# Week 5 Stop at the delivery strip

> [Download the Word version](W05_marker_Speaker_Notes.docx) · This Markdown copy is generated from the DOCX. Update the DOCX, then run `python scripts/sync_documents.py --write` from the repository root. Print layout, page breaks, headers/footers, and writing-space height remain in Word.

Speaker notes for the one-hour class. Prepare both kits and the printed fields before students arrive.

### Class setup

**Goal**  Each team calibrates a floor sensor, builds a removable tipping tray and uses it to unload a lightweight cube into a bay after a full stop. Record the sensor result and cargo result separately.

**Print**  Print W05\_Class\_Print\_Packet.pdf once on US Letter at Actual Size, single-sided, with auto orientation. Join tiles A, B and C with aligned ticks and tape behind the seams. Use the included movable strip and mission cards.

**Distance demo**  Load W05\_distance\_demo.py separately on one kit. Use a broad square wall with distance sensor on C. Start about 30 cm away measured from the sensor face. Rehearse 150 mm and 200 mm from the same start, then switch that robot back to the marker program.

**Lane and tray rehearsal**  Assemble both lanes before class. Rehearse M at 25 cm and the full strip-removed L run on both kits. Start with sensor D about 1–2 cm above the surface. Check light, dark and seam readings. With a mentor tray and cube fitted, test the loaded stop and tip. Mark each bay with flat, light-colored corner tabs outside the sensor path.

## Slide 1 Stop at the delivery strip

**Timing**  0–5 minutes

**Open**  Show the level tray with one foam or paper cube. Tip it by lifting the rear tab. Ask what tells the robot where to stop before anyone unloads it.

**Mission**  The hub shows M when the sensor finds the strip. Wait until the robot fully stops. Lift the tab and score whether the cube ends fully inside the bay.

## Slide 2 What tells the robot to stop

**Timing**  5–10 minutes

**Demo**  From the same marked start about 30 cm from the wall, run W05\_distance\_demo.py once with stop\_mm = 150 and once with stop\_mm = 200. Ask for predictions first. Compare actual stops using a ruler from the sensor face. The 200 mm threshold should stop the robot earlier and farther from the wall.

**Explain**  For a valid reading, gap &lt;= stop\_mm is the near-wall condition. Negative readings are handled as invalid. The moving helper checks between short moves and has a limit. If the demo is not rehearsed, show stationary gap readings and ask what the code would do.

**Transition**  Switch the demo robot to W05\_marker.py before rotations. A floor marker uses the same read-and-compare pattern with reflection instead of distance.

## Slide 3 Choose a threshold from readings

**Timing**  10–14 minutes

**Measure**  Keep the wheels still. Use the actual assembled lane and strip to show what the sensor prints over light and dark. The values on the slide are examples. Have teams record two readings on each surface and choose a whole number above both dark readings and below both light readings.

**Predict**  With a threshold of 40, ask what happens at 12, at 72 and at exactly 40. Only 12 counts as dark because the rule is reading &lt; threshold. A reading of 40 leaves another short move if any remain.

**Connect to code**  In W05\_marker.py the student recipe passes threshold to seek\_marker. The helper checks reflection before short moves, then checks after the last move. Keep the full program.

## Slide 4 Prepared lane and station swap

**Timing**  14–26 and 26–38 minutes

**Rotate**  14–26: T1/T3 calibrate on the prepared lanes and T2/T4 build trays. 26–38: swap. The build-first teams get the same baseline. Rotate the three jobs every four minutes.

**Robot station**  Center sensor D at START. Align the strip’s near edge at 25 cm. Read light and dark twice with wheels still, pick a threshold and record the baseline result. Both groups do this before any team tray goes on the robot.

**Build table**  Give each team stiff card or spare LEGO, a matched mounting proxy or base, rail pieces, tape and a lightweight cube. Follow slide 5. Have the builder, parts manager and tester each take a turn. Label the build for the retest.

**Lane reference**  W05\_Delivery\_Strip\_Full\_Size\_Field.pdf pages 2–4 make the 24 × 60 cm lane. Page 5 is the cutout. The diagram shows the order of the tiles. The paper center is blank so the sensor path stays clear of marking ink.

## Slide 5 Build a tray that unloads

**Timing**  38–44 minutes T1/T3, then 44–50 minutes T2/T4

**Build and hand-test**  Hinge the tray at the front and let that edge project past the chassis. Add short side rails, a rear support and a lift tab. Keep the front open. On the proxy, move it level with the cube, then lift the tab and try to land the cube in a paper bay. Improve one thing.

**Loaded retest**  T1/T3 retest at 38–44 and T2/T4 at 44–50. Check fit and clearance on the stopped robot. Keep the 25 cm strip, same sensor start and calibrated threshold. After M and a full stop, lift the rear tab. Record separately whether M occurred with the sensor over the strip and whether the cube stayed aboard and ends fully in the bay. L is the move limit.

**Stretch challenge**  After a successful manual delivery, add a short side lever to lift the back of the tray. Hand-test the loaded proxy against a shallow card ramp beside the strip. Position the ramp so only the lever contacts it and the cube releases near the measured stop. Tape the ramp down. The mentor must approve chassis, wheel, sensor and runout clearance before a powered try.

## Slide 6 Explain why the robot stopped

**Timing**  50–54 reflection and 54–60 save and reset

**Ask**  Did the strip stop the robot? Did the cube stay aboard and land in the bay? Ask each child to explain one of those observations or a tray change that helped.

**Carry forward**  Save the team project, actual trial results and both measured surface ranges. Keep each kit’s threshold as a starting point for the Week 6 rescue attachment. Recheck it after the attachment is mounted.
